title: Abusing the Winspace G3 Off Road

takeaways.text: After about 200–250 km of road riding the owner found a familiar road-race position and fairly quick steering despite the 70.5° head angle; on wet winter gravel and singletrack it was less comfortable and compliant than the previous G2, a trade he accepts for the handling.
Unlike his G2, whose D-shaped steerer let the headset loosen on rough rides, the G3's round steerer and larger bearings kept the headset tight.
The tapered seat-clamp wedge let the seatpost slip on the first hard rock; carbon assembly paste and 13 Nm torque cured it, and he suggests Winspace switch to a two-bolt clamp.

disclosure: The description says the Winspace and other product links are affiliate links.
summary: Off-road follow-up after about 250 km of road riding: position, steering feel, headset security compared with the G2, and a saddle clamp that slipped until re-torqued.
